Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>

title: Automating inequality? Gender bias in AI-mediated labor markets.
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly entering labor markets, with large language models (LLMs) now used to help write CVs and evaluate applicants. We study the risks this creates in a series of audit experiments in which applicant gender is randomly assigned while all other information is held constant. We find that LLMs generate gender-stereotypical CVs and exhibit gender bias in screening scores and wage recommendations. Screening scores track occupational gender segregation, penalizing women in male-dominated occupations and favoring them in female-dominated ones. Wage recommendations track occupational gender wage gaps when gender is explicit in the prompt, though this gradient weakens under name-based gender signaling and is sensitive to the LLMs being used. These disparities arise through two channels: evaluation bias, when identical CV content is evaluated differently by gender, and generation bias, when gendered content produced by the model affects later evaluation. Because the same systems shape both CV content and its subsequent assessment, these channels can reinforce one another. Taken together, our findings identify measurable risks of algorithmic amplification in AI-mediated job search.

title: Red Teaming a Patient-Facing Clinical AI Platform: 2-Phase Prospective Study.
abstract: Health systems are increasingly deploying patient-facing conversational AI platforms, yet validated methodologies for safety evaluation under realistic high-risk conditions are lacking. Prior work has documented safety failures in clinical AI but not shown whether iterative, health system-embedded testing can produce measurable safety improvement. This study aimed to evaluate a structured red teaming methodology for the safety assessment of a patient-facing clinical AI platform and determine whether targeted remediation guided by initial testing reduced safety failures in subsequent rounds of high-risk evaluations. A 2-phase prospective simulation study was conducted at a single academic health system in January and February 2026. Phase 1 enrolled 48 health care professionals who completed 6 randomized clinical scenarios (3 medium risk and 3 high risk). Following independent platform remediation informed by aggregated phase 1 findings, phase 2 enrolled 27 additional participants who completed 8 targeted high-risk scenarios. All 476 transcripts were independently scored by 3 calibrated raters using a 5-domain safety rubric. A strict firewall separated the research team from the platform developer, and only aggregated, deidentified findings were shared between phases. In phase 1, the high-risk failure rate was 30.2% (35/116) of transcripts vs 5.6% (7/126) for medium-risk scenarios. In phase 2, the high-risk failure rate was 8.5% (20/234), representing an absolute difference of 21.7 percentage points (participant-clustered 95% CI 11.1-32.2) and a 72% relative difference, with comparable performance across prespecified and improvised prompts within the targeted failure categories. Interrater reliability was moderate to strong in phase 1 (intraclass correlation coefficient=0.66, 95% CI 0.62-0.69) and moderate in phase 2 (intraclass correlation coefficient=0.49, 95% CI 0.43-0.55). Agreement on the binary failure classification remained stable between phases (Fleiss κ=0.70 in both phases), with observed agreement increasing from 90.9% (220/242) to 94.9% (222/234). Residual failures clustered around triage calibration errors and scope violations. Structured iterative red teaming was associated with improved safety performance on new high-risk scenarios following targeted remediation. The 5-domain rubric and scenario taxonomy offer a replicable methodology for health systems conducting predeployment and ongoing clinical AI safety assessment.

title: Eliciting Reader Preferences for Automated Systematic Gray Literature Reviews: Best-Worst Scaling Study.
abstract: Automation can be a useful efficiency tool for saving time in systematic reviews, but a trust gap and a steep learning curve persist concerning its accuracy and ease of use. It remains unknown whether these adoption barriers apply to the more complex process of systematic gray literature reviews (SGLRs), especially given the rapid evolution of large language models. This study seeks to identify the preferred features of SGLRs generated using an automation tool (automated SGLRs). Participants aged 18 years or older with experience using evidence from systematic reviews were recruited. A cross-sectional online Best-Worst Scaling Questionnaire was distributed through the authors' contacts, professional networks, and social media platforms. Descriptive statistics and multinomial logistic regression were used to estimate the baseline model for preferred features of automated SGLRs, while mixed logit analyses were used to explore subgroup heterogeneity. A total of 168 respondents, comprising researchers, academicians, health care professionals, health policymakers, and postgraduates, completed the study. Multinomial logistic regression found that the top 3 preferred features for automated SGLRs were (1) high precision and sensitivity comparable to manual methods (best-worst [BW] score 269, and M-logit estimate  The study concludes that automation tool developers should prioritize the accuracy of automated SGLRs, ensure algorithmic transparency, and integrate human-in-the-loop processes, as respondents most strongly preferred these features, which may support user trust.

title: Patient Perspectives on a Symptom Assessment App in Emergency Care: Interview Study Among Patients in the AkuSym Trial.
abstract: Symptom assessment apps (SAAs) allow laypersons to input their medical history and symptoms, generating a report of probable diagnoses and recommending next steps for medical care. Numerous and varied research findings exist regarding their diagnostic and triage accuracy, usability, acceptance, and user characteristics, including use in various settings. However, the perspective of low-acuity emergency patients on the benefits and challenges of using SAAs has not yet been explored. This study aimed to explore patients' experiences and attitudes toward the use of SAA before consultation in the emergency department (ED) and to identify perceived benefits and challenges of integrating SAAs into emergency care from the patients' perspective. We conducted semistructured interviews with self-referred, walk-in patients at 2 EDs and an ED-associated outpatient on-call practice in Berlin, who were allocated to the intervention group of the AkuSym trial. Participants had self-assessed their health complaints using the Ada Health SAA before their first encounter with the treating physician. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with deductively and inductively developed categories. Eighteen patients were interviewed between July 2022 and November 2022. Most participants stated that they would use an SAA again, including outside the emergency care setting. Key factors influencing reuse were precise symptom queries and clear, layperson-friendly medical content. Patients' trust in medical professionals was higher than in SAA assessments, and personal doctor-patient contact remained essential. The SAA was perceived primarily as a source of preliminary information and a supplement to doctor-patient contact. It helped participants reflect on and articulate their symptoms. Participants also saw potential for SAAs to support decisions about whether and where to seek medical care, to provide self-help recommendations for minor complaints, and to enable more informed participation in diagnostic discussions. Concerns included inaccurate or incomplete symptom input, difficulties understanding and interpreting SAA results, and receiving alarming or unclear information that could increase anxiety or complicate the subsequent consultation. Identified challenges included enabling information transfer through digital interfaces and ensuring data protection. Participants suggested solutions such as voluntary access via waiting-room QR codes, linking SAA reports to electronic patient records, and guiding patients to appropriate health care services. Meaningful integration of SAA use into emergency care requires a clear understanding of how SAA assessments should be used during the doctor-patient consultation, and ensuring accessibility for patients with limited digital health literacy. Such tools have the potential to improve health literacy and empower patients, potentially leading to more efficient health care use. Linking SAA reports to a public website that provides evidence-based, layperson-friendly information and contact details for appropriate health care providers could help patients understand their results and identify suitable care options.

title: Medical Interview Performance Using an AI-Based Standardized Patient vs a Human Standardized Patient: Randomized Crossover Trial.
abstract: In Japan, standardized patients (SPs) have traditionally been recruited to teach medical interview competencies. Recent advances in large language models have enabled increasingly natural conversational interactions, raising the possibility of using AI-based SPs (AI-SPs) for medical interview training. However, medical interview performance during interactions with AI-SPs compared with human SPs remains insufficiently understood. This randomized single-center crossover trial aimed to compare medical interview performance and learner-reported experiences between encounters with a large language model-based AI-SP and a human SP. Participants were fifth-year medical students undertaking clinical clerkships at Chiba University Hospital. The AI-SP was a text-based simulated patient implemented using GPT-4o. Participants were randomized to AI-SP followed by human SP, or the reverse. A washout period of at least 3 days was set between conditions. Each participant completed 2 cases, depression and appendicitis, in both conditions. For the AI-SP interviews, chat logs were retained, and a physician provided feedback after completion of the 2 cases. Human SP interviews were video recorded, and the physician portraying the SP provided feedback immediately after each interview. Medical interview performance was assessed using selected items from the Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX), with ratings performed independently by 2 general medicine specialists. Participants completed a self-rated questionnaire (7-point Likert-type scale) regarding learning satisfaction, perceived rapport formation, and active engagement in history taking. Forty-eight participants were analyzed. The Mini-CEX-based mean total score was significantly higher for the human SP than for the AI-SP (23.9, SD 1.7 vs 22.7, SD 1.7, respectively; mean difference 1.24; t Medical interview performance differed between the 2 SP conditions, with higher history taking and overall clinical competence scores in the human SP condition. The text-based nature of the AI-SP and the absence of nonverbal cues may have contributed to these differences. Although no significant differences between conditions were observed in most other assessment outcomes, learning satisfaction, or perceived rapport, self-rated active engagement in history taking was higher with the AI-SP condition. AI-SPs may offer a complementary modality for medical interview practice; however, this study assessed performance during simulated encounters rather than subsequent learning gains or performance with real patients. title: Structural Determinants of Conformational Diversity in OXA Carbapenemases.
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAb) is a global health threat with limited therapeutic options. Antibiotic resistance is primarily driven by the expression of carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D β-lactamases (CHDLs), with clinically prevalent variants belonging to the OXA-23-like (OXA-23, OXA-146, OXA-225, and OXA-239), OXA-24-like (OXA-24 and OXA-160), and OXA-58-like (OXA-58) subfamilies. To explore the structural dynamics within and across these subfamilies, we employed reinforcement learning-driven enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics simulations integrated with convolutional variational autoencoders (CVAE) and BindSiteS-CNN model. Our CVAE-based deep learning analysis reveals that variants within the same subfamily exhibit distinct dynamic behavior, particularly in the B5B6-Loop, which are consistent with experimentally reported differences in substrate profiles and catalytic efficiency. The BindSiteS-CNN model further resolves the local active-site dynamics across the parent enzymes, offering insights into the structural features that distinguish these CHDL subfamilies. The results presented here highlight how global and local conformational dynamics differ across major CHDL families and provide structural insights for interpreting experimentally observed differences in substrate specificity and catalytic behavior in CRAb.

title: Image-guided and augmented reality-assisted robotic surgery.
abstract: Image-guided and augmented-reality (AR)-assisted robotic surgery is moving from static preoperative visualization toward dynamic, automated navigation. This review summarizes evidence from the past 12-18 months on three-dimensional (3D) virtual models, AR, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted registration in robotic urology, focusing on which applications have moved to comparative and randomized evidence, and on how far this rationale now generalizes beyond the centers that first described it. In radical prostatectomy, a randomized trial of AI-driven 3D-AR guidance vs. cognitive MRI guidance showed lower overall positive margins, less postoperative radiotherapy, and better 12-month continence. In partial nephrectomy, 3D models have progressed from anatomical planning to perfusion-mapped clamping and automated AI-based registration, with favorable outcomes across comparative, meta-analytic, and propensity-matched series, including in horseshoe kidneys and totally endophytic tumors. Independent European groups have reported automated registration, segmentation, and nephrometry tools, and small series have extended image guidance to kidney transplantation, vena cava thrombectomy, upper tract urothelial carcinoma, and testicular cancer surgery. Randomized evidence in prostatectomy, a maturing pathway in partial nephrectomy, and growing independent replication support an expanding but still procedure-limited role for image-guided robotic surgery. Standardized protocols, objective accuracy metrics, multicenter validation, and structured training remain necessary before wider adoption.

title: Frequency-Specific Thalamocortical Network Dynamics During Focal Seizures in Humans.
abstract: The thalamus is an emerging neuromodulation target in drug-resistant focal epilepsy because of its frequent ictal involvement. However, frequency-specific and directional thalamocortical dynamics remain poorly understood. We sought to characterize thalamocortical network dynamics across seizure evolution using stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). We retrospectively analyzed SEEG recordings from patients with pediatric-onset drug-resistant focal epilepsy with simultaneous cortical and thalamic sampling focusing on the anterior nucleus (AN) and centromedian nucleus (CM). We applied visual analysis with quantitative measures of spectral power, imaginary coherence, and spectral Granger causality across slow (1-12 Hz), β (13-30 Hz), and γ (30-70 Hz) bands to quantify thalamocortical and cortico-cortical interactions from seizure onset to termination. Random forest models were trained to classify seizure state using thalamic EEG features as an exploratory analysis. The final cohort comprised 19 patients (median age, 16.9 years; 31.6% female), with 66 focal seizures analyzed. Thalamic ictal activity was present at seizure onset in 81% of sampled thalamic contacts and became nearly universal by seizure termination. Both the thalamus and seizure onset zone showed increased spectral power during seizures, with prominent slow-band augmentation at seizure termination in the thalamus. Similarly, thalamocortical imaginary coherence increased during seizures, with the largest changes near seizure termination in the slow band (AN-SOZ: 11% [IQR, 2 to 20], rank-biserial correlations (rrb) = 0.84; CM-SOZ: 12% [IQR, 3 to 23], rrb = 0.84) and β band (AN-SOZ: 5% [IQR, 0 to 12], rrb = 0.74; CM-SOZ: 8% [IQR, 2 to 15], rrb = 0.86). Directed connectivity analyses demonstrated bidirectional thalamocortical interactions, with large slow-frequency thalamus-to-SOZ outflow near seizure termination from both AN and CM, exceeding propagation-zone-to-SOZ cortico-cortical flow (both  Human focal seizures engage frequency-specific and bidirectional thalamocortical interactions that evolve from onset to termination. These findings support the thalamus as a source of clinically relevant seizure-state information and may inform thalamic biomarker development for neuromodulation in drug-resistant epilepsy.

FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
abstract: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.
ai_summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury . These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy .

title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
abstract: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.
